title: Query Lower Bounds for Diffusion Sampling: Proposition E.1
author: Zhiyang Xun, Eric Price
work: Query Lower Bounds for Diffusion Sampling
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition E.1 (source0.tex lines 1703--1720, source label prop:bounded-reweighting), that the paper's hard query-lower-bound construction survives replacing the uniform sampling measure by any deterministic probability vector whose sup-norm is polynomially bounded in the dimension, and also survives a random weight family drawn independently of the algorithm, delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1722--1770 (49 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The proposition is the robustness statement that lets the paper's lower bound cover non-uniform hard instances rather than only the uniform one. The proof is a genuine multi-step argument: it re-derives the moment and score bounds of the weighted hard law from the bounded-weight hypothesis, controls the reweighted densities and their normalising constants, and re-runs the comparison against the uniform hard law through the article's dense-codebook and blind-output tools. H2: a complete original research-paper proposition with a fully written proof of moderate length whose steps (weighted moment comparison, density control, reduction to the uniform hard law) are not routine verifications.
